body.en: α-*Amino acids*, $H_2N-CHR-COOH$, have –NH₂ and –COOH on the same carbon. Essential amino acids (e.g. valine, leucine, lysine) must come from the diet; non-essential ones the body makes. In solution an amino acid exists as a dipolar ion (zwitterion), $H_3N^+-CHR-COO^-$, so it is amphoteric and has a high melting point. All except glycine are optically active, with the L-configuration.
body.kn: ಅಮೈನೊ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಮೇಲೆ ಅಮೈನೊ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲ್ ಗುಂಪುಗಳಿವೆ. ನೀರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಅವು ಎರಡೂ ಆವೇಶಗಳಿರುವ ಜ್ವಿಟ್ಟರ್ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಉಭಯಧರ್ಮೀಯ. ಗ್ಲೈಸಿನ್ ಹೊರತು ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ದೃಕ್ ಸಕ್ರಿಯ.

say.en: An alpha-amino acid has the amino group and the carboxyl group on the same carbon. The side chain R decides which amino acid it is.
In water an amino acid exists as a zwitterion: the acid group gives its proton to the amino group. So it behaves both as an acid and a base.
Amino acids join by peptide bonds: the COOH of one and the NH₂ of the next lose water.
Proteins have four levels of structure, from the sequence up to how separate chains fit together.

say.en: Heat or a change of pH breaks the hydrogen bonds: the protein is denatured, but its sequence stays. Think of a boiled egg.

narration.en: In water an amino acid is a zwitterion, H₃N⁺–CHR–COO⁻. In acid it gains H⁺ (net +), in alkali it loses H⁺ (net −). In an electric field the molecules drift toward the electrode of opposite charge; at the isoelectric point they stay put.

body.en: The peptide bond –CO–NH– joins amino acids; n amino acids form a chain with n − 1 peptide bonds. A polypeptide with more than about a hundred residues (molar mass above 10,000 u) is a *protein*. Fibrous proteins (keratin, myosin) are long and insoluble; globular proteins (insulin, albumins) are folded and soluble. Primary structure: the sequence. Secondary: α-helix or β-pleated sheet, held by hydrogen bonds. Tertiary: overall folding, held by hydrogen bonds, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces. Quaternary: arrangement of subunits (haemoglobin has four).
body.kn: ಪೆಪ್ಟೈಡ್ ಬಂಧಗಳು ಅಮೈನೊ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಪಳಿಯಾಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಕ್ರಮಾನುಗತಿ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ರಚನೆ, ಹೆಲಿಕ್ಸ್ ಮತ್ತು ಹಾಳೆಗಳು ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ, ಒಟ್ಟು ಮಡಚುವಿಕೆ ತೃತೀಯಕ, ಹಲವು ಸರಪಳಿಗಳ ಜೋಡಣೆ ಚತುರ್ಥಕ ರಚನೆ.

narration.en: Peptide bonds link amino acids into chains. The sequence is the primary structure, helices and sheets are the secondary structure, the overall fold is tertiary, and the packing of several chains is quaternary.

body.en: A change of temperature or pH disturbs the hydrogen bonds; the globules unfold and the helices uncoil, and the protein loses its biological activity. Secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed but the primary structure remains. Examples: the egg white setting on boiling; milk curdling when bacteria make lactic acid.
body.kn: ಶಾಖ ಅಥವಾ ಆಮ್ಲ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಅನ್ನು ಬಿಚ್ಚಿ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ ಮತ್ತು ತೃತೀಯಕ ರಚನೆ ನಾಶ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ; ಕ್ರಮಾನುಗತಿ ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಬೇಯಿಸಿದ ಮೊಟ್ಟೆ ಮತ್ತು ಒಡೆದ ಹಾಲು ಉದಾಹರಣೆಗಳು.

narration.en: Net charge of glycine against pH: charge = 1/(1 + 10^(pH − pKa₁)) − 1/(1 + 10^(pKa₂ − pH)). At the isoelectric point pI = (pKa₁ + pKa₂)/2 the net charge is zero. Set pH = 1: glycine is almost entirely the cation, charge +1. Slide to pH 5.97 (the pI): the net charge is zero, and glycine would not move in an electric field. narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the molar mass of the dipeptide glycylalanine (Gly–Ala). Glycine = 75 g/mol, alanine = 89 g/mol.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the molar mass of the dipeptide glycylalanine (Gly-Ala). Glycine equals 75 grams per mole, alanine equals 89 grams per mole.
One peptide bond forms, releasing one H 2O 18 grams per mole.
Molar mass equals 75 plus 89 minus 18 equals 146 grams per mole.
So the answer is 146 grams per mole.

say.en: Let us solve this together. How many different tripeptides can be made from glycine, alanine and valine if each is used exactly once? How many peptide bonds does each contain?
The order matters (Gly-Ala-Val differs from Val-Ala-Gly).
Number of sequences equals 3! = 3 times 2 times 1 equals 6.
A chain of 3 amino acids has 3 minus 1 equals 2 peptide bonds.
So the answer is 6 tripeptides, each with 2 peptide bonds.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. On denaturation of a protein, which structure remains intact?
Heat or a change of pH breaks hydrogen bonds and other weak forces, unfolding the secondary and tertiary structure.
The covalent peptide bonds, and so the amino-acid sequence primary structure, survive.
